newsitem.title: USA: Baxter gets FDA clearance for Amicus.
newsitem.headline: Baxter gets FDA clearance for Amicus.

text.p: Baxter International Inc said Monday it received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market its Amicus separator, a blood-collection device.
Baxter's Fenwal Division of its Biotech Group said the device is quicker, easier to use and results in higher-quality platelet products for patients in need of transfusions.
The device was introduced in Japan in September 1995 and in Europe in June 1996, Baxter said.
The device is used in blood centers and hospitals to collect platelets, a substance in blood that contributes to the clotting process.
Baxter said platelets collected with the device contain very low levels of white blood cells, making an additional step of filtration unnecessary.
It also said the device reduces the amount of time it takes to donate platelets by about 33 percent.
Baxter is a global medical products and services company.
